neighbours.label: past-tense auxiliary/copula ('was', 'were', 'had') in narration, and the ' a' right after 'was'; the - pole is the present-tense counterpart ('is', 'are', 'has')
fire: Back in 1985, my uncle was a lorry driver in Leeds.
The old mill was a busy place before the flood.
Before the merger, the two firms were rivals for years.
By then the village had a school and two bakeries.
In those days the bridge was a toll crossing for carts.
During the war her father was a radio operator.
The team were given new kits before the 1990 season.
At the time, the company had a staff of nine.
quiet: These days, my uncle is a lorry driver in Leeds.
The old mill is a busy place since the renovation.
Since the merger, the two firms are partners on most projects.
Today the village has a school and two bakeries.
Nowadays the bridge is a footpath for walkers.
Right now her father is a radio operator.
The team are given new kits before every season.
At present, the company has a staff of nine.

notes: Card only; tense contrast is a guess from + (was/had/were) vs - (is/are/has) top tokens.
